content: Don Pepín García is a premium cigar brand that is handcrafted and owned by El Rey de los Habanos, Inc. The brand was established by José Pepín García and is produced in two locations: the El Rey de los Habanos factory in Little Havana, Miami, Florida, and the Tabacalera Cubana factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. The cigars under this brand are categorized into three distinct ranges, each offering varying strengths. All cigars are made using Nicaraguan tobaccos in different blends. The boxes are stamped with a date code to indicate their production time. Don Pepín García Blue Label The Blue Label was the first range introduced by the brand, followed by the Serie JJ. It includes six different vitolas and one limited-edition release, the Lancero. These cigars are full-bodied and are not recommended for novice smokers. The wrapper is an oily Nicaraguan Corojo leaf, which has a cinnamon-like color. The cigars are packaged in cedar boxes containing 25 cigars each. Initially, they were uncelloed, but as of the summer of 2007, they are celloed. The band design features a blue background with gold lettering. The center of the band displays Don Pepín García in gold on a blue field, surrounded by a red and gold border. Below the name is a reduced version of Don Pepín's signature. The band also includes the U.S. and Cuban flags within roundels on each side. Ratings and Awards The Invictos vitola received a rating of 88 in the August 2006 issue of Cigar Aficionado magazine. The Magnate vitola was rated 89 in the February 2007 issue of Cigar Aficionado magazine. Don Pepín García Black Edition (Cuban Classic/Black Label) The Black Edition is the newest range in the brand and was introduced for national distribution in the United States in late 2006. These cigars are manufactured at the Tabacalera Cubana factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. They are uncelloed and packaged in cedar cabinets containing 20 cigars. A colored ribbon surrounds the cigars, and a label with Don Pepín García and a facsimile of his signature is attached. The band design is similar to the Blue Label but features a black background. Additionally, there is a second band with gold borders on a black background, displaying the words Cuban Classic in gold. The sides of the box are stamped with 20 / Don Pepín (in script) / ♦ BLACK EDITION ♦ / frontmark. The bottom of the box is stamped with the month and year of manufacture. Ratings and Awards The entire range underwent a vertical tasting in the May 22, 2007 issue of Cigar Insider. The 1979 vitola received the highest rating of 92, while the 1973 vitola received the lowest rating of 85. The 1952 vitola was rated 88, and the 1950, 1970, and 1977 vitolas each received a rating of 89. Don Pepín García Serie JJ (White Label) The Serie JJ range was developed collaboratively by Don Pepín García and his son, Jaime García. These cigars are mediumto full-bodied and feature a light-brown Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper. They are packaged in plain boxes containing 24 cigars, except for the Salomon vitola, which is packaged in boxes of five. The band design is similar to the Blue Label but features a white background with a red border. There is also a second, straight band that is white and displays Serie JJ in print. The Salomon vitolas are exclusively rolled by Don Pepín García himself.
